method: Real CBM queries (mcp__codebase-memory-mcp__trace_path / search_graph) against the actual indexed Kokoro-FastAPI checkout, read live during this experiment -- not re-derived from Sydes' own CBMClient plumbing, but the same underlying graph Sydes' CBM backend would supply as call_edges/usage_edges. Project: Users-ksnaik-sample_repos-Kokoro-FastAPI. Cases 1-6 queried on branch py-real-01-max-output-duration (the branch actually indexed); cases 7-8 queried against the SAME index, justified because api/src/services/audio.py, api/src/services/tts_service.py, and the _process_chunk call chain are baseline files untouched by either PR6 or PR7 and are identical across both branches.

cases.cross_check: trace_path(model_status, outbound, depth=3) -> callees_total=3, exhaustive: ModelManager.status/_auto_unload_enabled/_auto_unload_timeout only
cases.notes: model_status is absent from generate_audio_stream's real, exhaustive (untruncated) inbound-caller set at depth 3, AND model_status's own real, exhaustive outbound callee set contains nothing related. Both directions checked, both complete.

cases.query: trace_path(generate_from_phonemes, outbound) -- name AMBIGUOUS: 2 real matches (route handler in development.py, TTSService method in tts_service.py). CBM itself refused to guess and returned suggestions.

result.known_gap: Manual source reading confirms the route handler DOES call `await tts_service.generate_from_phonemes(...)` (an instance method on a locally-scoped variable). This real call is ABSENT from CBM's own traced callee list -- a genuine, empirically-confirmed graph incompleteness for this exact handler, not merely a theoretical caveat.

cases.notes: Fails the completeness certificate on its own stated terms ('all relevant direct calls in the handler are structurally extracted') -- independently verified false for this handler. The manual oracle still says FALSE (TTSService.generate_from_phonemes calls backend._get_pipeline().generate_from_tokens, never generate_audio_stream), but the GRAPH cannot honestly certify that; it is silent about a call it doesn't even represent. Reported as GRAPH_UNKNOWN, not GRAPH_HAS_STRONG_NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE, precisely because of this rule.
Exhaustive (16/16, no truncation signal), covers model_manager/kokoro_v1 methods and one unrelated web AudioService.cancel call. No path to generate_audio/generate_audio_stream.

result.max_output_duration_s_field_node: DOES NOT EXIST as a separate node

cases.notes: Not merely an unmodeled RELATION -- the intermediate NODES needed to represent this chain (the type alias, the validator function) were never created by CBM's own extractor for this file/shape. Feeding Sydes' generic _FactIndex traversal real CBM edges cannot rescue this: there is nothing to feed it. This is empirically confirmed, not inferred from the schema docstring alone.
Same finding as case 5, sharing the same missing node.

cases.query: trace_path(convert_audio, inbound, depth=3) and trace_path(_process_chunk, outbound, depth=2)
cases.notes: convert_audio IS reachable from POST /audio/speech (3 hops via create_speech -> generate_audio_stream -> _process_chunk -> convert_audio) -- that part is TRUE. What's FALSE is any relation from the changed normalizer symbols (handle_url/handle_email/_speak_url_symbols) to convert_audio: _process_chunk's real, exhaustive (20/20) callee list contains no normalizer-related symbol. Both neighborhoods (convert_audio's callers, _process_chunk's callees) are exhaustively enumerated with no truncation signal.

cases.query: same as case 7 (trim_audio is called from the same _process_chunk, already checked exhaustively)
cases.notes: Same evidence and reasoning as case 7.

summary.note_on_case_2: CBM's own trace_path tool refused to silently guess between the two same-named symbols and returned an explicit ambiguous status with disambiguation suggestions -- a real, working safety mechanism already present in the tool, not something this experiment had to build.
